confirmations: EARFCN->band mapping is CORRECT for nearly all observed EARFCNs. Recomputed every unique (earfcn,band,center) tuple in origin_records.json against TS 36.101 Table 5.7.3-1 (DL center = FDL_low + 0.1*(N - NOffs-DL)): EARFCN 100/275/475 -> B1 (2120.0/2137.5/2157.5 MHz); 1350/1550/1694 -> B3 (1820.0/1840.0/1854.4 MHz); 2500/2600 -> B5 (879.0/889.0 MHz); 2850/3200 -> B7 (2630.0/2665.0 MHz); 3600/3650/3743 -> B8 (940.0/945.0/954.3 MHz). All match the records exactly. The task's spot-check 3200->B7 is confirmed.
PLMN->operator names are CORRECT. MCC 450 = South Korea; 450/05 = SK Telecom, 450/08 = KT. Records label these accordingly (by_operator: SK Telecom 450/05 x39, KT 450/08 x1).

q-RxLevMin decode is CORRECT. Raw CSV lte-rrc_q_rxlevmin_show stores the magnitude as a positive integer (observed set 55,57,61,62,64,65,66,70). Per TS 36.331 the q-RxLevMin IE is INTEGER(-70..-22) in 2 dBm steps, so actual dBm = 2 * field = -2 * stored_magnitude. value 64 -> -128 dBm. Every record's q_rxlevmin_dbm equals -2*value (verified for all 8 distinct values). value 70 -> -140 dBm sits at the spec floor and is valid.

RAT classification logic is sound. Records carry an explicit rat object {lte_rrc, nr_rrc, nas_eps_4g, nas_5gs}. The 33 '5G-NSA / LTE+NR' files all show lte_rrc=true AND nr_rrc=true AND nas_5gs=false (NR RRC present alongside LTE/EPS NAS, no 5GS NAS = NSA), e.g. normal_2026_04_30_14_03_33.csv, normal_mixed1.csv. This correctly distinguishes LTE (lte_rrc only), 5G-NSA (lte_rrc+nr_rrc, EPS NAS), and 5G-SA (nas_5gs present). Raw scan confirms nas-5gs_security_header_type appears only 6 times across 133 files, consistent with the single '5G' file.

nas-eps security_header_type values match TS 24.301 5.1.1: 0 = plain (not security protected), 1 = integrity protected, 2 = integrity protected and ciphered, 3 = integrity protected with new EPS security context, 4 = integrity protected and ciphered with new EPS security context. The raw CSV directly confirms value 2 with showname 'Security header type: Integrity protected and ciphered (2)' (662 occurrences). All of 0,1,2,3,4 are observed in the data.

cellbarred decode is CORRECT. Raw lte-rrc_cellbarred_show is consistently '1' (1379 rows). Per TS 36.331 cellBarred is ENUMERATED {barred(0), notBarred(1)}, so 1 = notBarred (cell is available for camping), matching live commercial/lab cells. Records store cellbarred '1' unchanged.

corrections.claimed: center_mhz 783.0 (nominal 700 MHz), in origin_records.json bands entries (50 files)
corrections.correct: center_mhz should be 778.0 MHz. Band assignment B28 and nominal '700 MHz' are correct; only the center frequency is wrong by +5 MHz.
corrections.evidence: TS 36.101 Table 5.7.3-1 Band 28: FDL_low=758.0 MHz, NOffs-DL=9210. DL center = 758.0 + 0.1*(9410-9210) = 758.0 + 20.0 = 778.0 MHz. The stored 783.0 MHz would correspond to EARFCN 9460, not 9410. (Note: raw CSV lte-rrc_dl_carrierfreq_showname shows '786', a separate parser-display artifact, neither 783 nor 778; the authoritative value from the EARFCN is 778.0.)

corrections.item: Carrier values 10737 and 10836 listed as 'earfcn' with band=None in the bands array
corrections.claimed: Treated as band-less entries in the frequency.bands list of 13 NSA records (origin_records.json), implicitly EARFCN-like
corrections.correct: These are NOT lte-rrc_dl_carrierfreq (serving DL EARFCN); they come from lte-rrc_carrierfreq (column 39/43, the SIB-type inter-frequency/measurement carrier field). 10737/10836 fall outside every LTE FDD DL EARFCN range in TS 36.101 (above Band 65 top 10359, below Band 66), so band=None is the only honest mapping and they must not be read as serving cells or decoded to a band/frequency. Confirmed band=None already, but the records mix this measurement-carrier field into the same 'bands' list as serving dl_carrierfreq values, which can mislead.
corrections.evidence: Raw scan of normal_2026_04_30_14_03_33.csv: value 10737 appears 43x only in column lte-rrc_carrierfreq_show, never in lte-rrc_dl_carrierfreq. No LTE DL band in TS 36.101 contains 10737 or 10836.

caveats: The single EARFCN-center error (9410 -> 783.0 instead of 778.0) does NOT change any origin classification: band assignment (B28) and the commercial/test verdicts depend on band number and PLMN/paging, not the exact MHz. Impact is cosmetic/reference-table accuracy only.

Field shownames in these CSVs are largely numeric node IDs (e.g. q_rxlevmin showname '285', cellbarred showname '202'), not human-readable text, an artifact of the parser. Decodes were therefore validated against the numeric 'show'/'value' codes plus 3GPP spec, with the one genuine text string available ('Integrity protected and ciphered (2)') corroborating the security_header_type=2 case.

nas-eps_security_header_type_show in the raw data also contains values 5,6,8,11,12,14,15 (beyond the 0-4 the task asks about). These are not extra security-header types; they are the EMM message-type / protocol-discriminator byte captured when the high nibble is mis-aligned for plain NAS messages. Only 0-4 are valid TS 24.301 security header types and only those were verified.

I could not reach the live 3GPP PDF in this environment; EARFCN, q-RxLevMin, security-header, and cellbarred decodes were verified by recomputation against the standard TS 36.101 / TS 36.331 / TS 24.301 tables from knowledge, cross-checked against the raw CSV values. The arithmetic and code-to-meaning mappings are deterministic and reproducible from the formulas shown.

confirmations: Split is internally consistent at 102 commercial / 31 test/lab. by_origin_reason sums to 102 commercial (58 LTE-attach-not-captured + 39 SKT + 1 KT + 4 foreign-paging) and 31 test/lab (4 PLMN-00101 + 3 Band-8 + 24 NR-no-identity). The 34 files labeled '5G-NSA/LTE+NR' or '5G' split as 24 test + 10 commercial; no file has an NR signal with a non-5G label.

Schema constraint verified: the CSV header has NO NR carrier ARFCN/freqband column. The only frequency fields are lte-rrc_carrierfreq and lte-rrc_dl_carrierfreq. So NR captures genuinely cannot be bound to a serving NR frequency/operator from the data, validating the premise of the band-substitution rule.

Band-8 test files data3/data4/data5 verified from raw CSV: only LTE EARFCN 3600 (=Band 8, range 3450-3799 via the _show decimal column), empty e212_gummei (no PLMN), zero paging records, zero IMSIs, no NR rows, no NAS-5GS. Pure Band-8 testbed. Labels correct.

PLMN-00101 test files data/data2/data6/data7 verified: e212_gummei_mcc=00f1 mnc=f110 (BCD => MCC 001, MNC 01), Band 8 (data6 also Band 28). PLMN 00101 wins over the stray commercial-band measurement. Labels correct.

24 NR test files have nr-rrc rows present, empty e212_gummei, no 450/xx PLMN, and no IMSI exposed except one anomaly (see corrections). Their heavy paging is by S-TMSI inside lte-rrc_pagingrecordlist (e212_imsi=-1 on those rows), so foreign_paged_count=0 by IMSI is defensible for 23 of them.

normal_5g_session_72 verified as the cleanest standalone-5G testbed capture: NAS-5GS present (6 rows), zero paging, no gummei PLMN, no IMSI, no SUCI, only a 5G-TMSI and an unreliable per-digit nr-rrc mcc=3. Correctly test/lab.

Point 2 confirmed decisively. The 10 commercial NR/5G-NSA files all carry gummei MCC 54f0 (=450, SKT/KT). The foreign-paging ones page IMSIs from Japan-440, China-460, Indonesia-510, Hong Kong-454, Thailand-520, Sri Lanka-413, Vietnam-452 alongside Korea-450 (e.g. 2026_04_20_14_35_18 pages 29 Japanese + 1 Chinese + 1 HK + 2 Indonesian IMSIs; 2026_04_30_15_08_32 pages 21 Chinese + 6 Sri Lankan + 4 Indonesian). A single provisioned 00101 SIM on an Open5GS lab core physically cannot page foreign roamers it never registered. These are genuine commercial cells; mixed17 (KT 450/08, touches Band 8) is correctly commercial because the 450 PLMN overrides the band.
normal_2026_04_20_14_35_18 (24 MB) pages 4411 distinct S-TMSIs plus foreign IMSIs, an unmistakable busy live commercial cell, anchoring the commercial paging baseline.

corrections.claimed: test/lab, reason 'NR n78/n79, no commercial identity' (origin_records.json reports foreign_paged_count=0, distinct_imsi=1)
corrections.correct: Should be commercial. Row 12 is an LTE-RRC paging message carrying e212_imsi 450050746404373 (hex-ascii 343530...), which decodes to MCC 450 MNC 05 = SK Telecom Korea, a third-party subscriber (not the auditor's 515/02 Globe SIM, not 00101). Per the stated override rule, paging a real 450/xx subscriber by IMSI marks the capture commercial. A 00101 testbed cannot page an SKT subscriber by IMSI.
corrections.evidence: raw CSV row 12, info=paging, e212_imsi_show=450050746404373; auditor own IMSI 515027302508642 differs. This makes the true split 103 commercial / 30 test/lab, and the NR-test bucket 23 not 24.

corrections.item: Ground-truth brief count of commercial NR files
corrections.claimed: 11 NR/5G-NSA files carry SKT/KT PLMN + foreign paging and are kept commercial
corrections.correct: Only 10 commercial files have an NR signal (9 SKT 450/05 + 1 KT 450/08 = mixed17). No 11th commercial file carries any NR or NAS-5GS signal. The '11' is off by one; the 102/31 totals in origin_records.json are still internally consistent.
corrections.evidence: Enumerated all records with rat_label in {5G-NSA/LTE+NR, 5G}: 34 total = 24 test + 10 commercial; no commercial record has nr_rrc/nas_5gs True outside those 10.

corrections.item: Brief claim that the 24 NR files have '(almost all) zero paged IMSIs'
corrections.claimed: the 24 NR files have NR present, no 450/xx PLMN, and almost all zero paged IMSIs
corrections.correct: Most NR test files have substantial paging, by S-TMSI not IMSI. Distinct paged S-TMSIs reach 57 (mixed16), 52 (mixed9), 49 (mixed18), 40 (udp_streaming7). 'Zero paged IMSIs' is true (no IMSI-level paging on 23 of 24) but 'zero paging' is false; the volume of distinct S-TMSIs is high.
corrections.evidence: lte-rrc_pagingrecordlist_value distinct counts per file; e212_imsi=-1 on those paging rows confirms S-TMSI paging.

caveats: Point 3 / strongest counter-argument to the 'NR + no commercial identity => n78/n79 testbed' rule: many of these NR files page DOZENS of distinct S-TMSIs (up to 57) and simultaneously measure commercial LTE bands B1/B3/B28 (e.g. mixed1 and udp_streaming5 measure B1+B3+B8+B28). A single-SIM srsRAN/Open5GS testbed pages essentially only its one UE, so high distinct-S-TMSI paging is the fingerprint of a busy LIVE commercial cell, not a quiet lab. Under this reading some 'NR test' files could be commercial 5G-NSA where the LTE anchor's PLMN simply was not captured (attach/SIB1 missed), with the dozens of paged identities being the cell's real idle population. The rule survives only because (a) the schema cannot bind the NR leg to an operator, (b) none of the 23 carry a 450/xx gummei or any IMSI, and (c) the LTE bands seen can be inter-frequency measurement/neighbor reporting rather than the serving cell. So the label is defensible but NOT airtight: it rests on absence-of-evidence (no captured PLMN) plus the dataset owner's provenance, not on positive proof of testbed origin. The high-paging files (mixed16/9/18, udp_streaming5/7, voltecall4) are the weakest test labels and the most likely candidates to actually be commercial 5G with the attach uncaptured.

Band classification depends on reading the EARFCN _show column (decimal), NOT the _value column. The _value field is the raw ASN.1-encoded bytes (e.g. 2038 for EARFCN 3600) and a naive hex/decimal parse of _value mislabels Band 8 as Band 4. All band figures here use _show.

gummei PLMN decoding relies on the BCD-with-f-filler convention: 00f1/f110 => 001/01, 54f0 => 450. Per the ground truth, per-digit lte-rrc/nr-rrc mcc/mnc fields are unreliable and were not used for operator identity; only e212_gummei and full e212_imsi were trusted.

The single mislabel (2026_05_14_14_31_43) appears to stem from the origin_records imsi_analysis pipeline not extracting the paged IMSI from that file (it shows distinct_imsi=1 but classified it test and set foreign_paged=0). If the dataset owner regenerates origin_records, that file should flip to commercial, shifting the split to 103/30 and the NR-test bucket to 23.

I spot-checked raw CSVs for all 3 Band-8 files, all 4 PLMN-00101 files, all 24 NR-test files (paging/IMSI/gummei/NR/NAS-5GS), 5g_session_72, and all 10 commercial NR files. I did not re-derive the 58 'attach not captured' or 39 SKT pure-LTE commercial labels beyond a paging spot-check, since they are not in scope for the band rule; those labels were taken as given.

confirmations: The '9 unknown RAT' files are real 3G/UMTS (UTRAN RRC) captures, NOT empty or corrupt, and NOT 'unknown'. In origin_records.json all nine carry rat_label '3G (UMTS)' (all four rat flags lte_rrc/nr_rrc/nas_eps_4g/nas_5gs = False), packet_type pure 'rrc'. Their raw info column holds genuine WCDMA RRC PDU names: 'Master Information Block', 'Sys Info Type SB1/1/3/5/11', 'Complete SIBshort', 'first/subsequent/last Segment', 'rrc Connection Request/Setup/Setup Complete/Release', 'paging Type1', 'integrity Check Info', 'measurement Control', 'downlink/uplink Direct Transfer'. The CSV schema has no UMTS-RRC columns (only lte-rrc/nr-rrc/nas-5gs), so the parser left those rows with only timestamp/packet_type/direction/info/e212_imsi populated. They label as 'unknown RAT' upstream only because none of the four schema RAT flags fire, but the message names are unambiguously 3G. Real data property.

The 3G origin classifications check out. normal_2026_04_13_15_26_14 pages IMSI 440207101965410 (MCC 440 = Japan, NTT DoCoMo) alongside SKT 450/05 subscribers, and normal_2026_04_15_16_16_44 pages IMSI 434054440348258 (MCC 434 = Uzbekistan) plus four 450/05 SKT IMSIs. A single 00101 testbed SIM cannot page foreign roamers, so these are genuine commercial 3G cells (origin_reason 'paging of foreign-roamer IMSIs on a live cell'). The remaining seven 3G files have no operator field and are classified commercial by the default-band rule (origin_reason 'LTE on commercial bands, attach not captured').

Duration outlier normal_2026_04_20_14_35_18 (~58392 s / 16.2 h) is a REAL long DIAG session, not a clock jump. The timestamp column is a per-file relative capture clock in seconds starting at 0.0. Across all 14,831 rows it is strictly monotonic (0 backward steps); the largest single forward gap is 277.8 s (idle stretch). The file is rich content (rrc 13664, nas 789, nas+rrc 378), serves on SKT gummei 450/05, and pages foreign roamers MCC 460/CN, 454/HK, 510/ID, 440/JP. Confirmed commercial, genuine 16 h capture.

The per-file timestamp clock is consistently relative and monotonic across the whole normal set: every one of the ~133 files starts at exactly 0.0, and only ONE file (normal_2026_05_14_15_22_36) has any backward step. So timestamp is a reliable monotonic capture clock; duration_s = max-min timestamp is trustworthy as elapsed session time.

The single 5G-only file normal_5g_session_72 is a genuine 5G standalone (SA) session, real data. 13 rows: NR-RRC Setup Request/Setup/SIB1/MIB/Release plus 5GS NAS Registration request, Deregistration request, Configuration update command, with 32 distinct nr-rrc_* fields actually populated (cellidentity, trackingareacode, cellbarred=1, timers t300/t310/t311/t319). No LTE anchor present, so it is 5G-SA, not NSA. It has no gummei and no full IMSI (no commercial identity), and its NR SIB1 only exposes the unreliable per-digit mcc_show=3/mnc_show=2 fragments, so test/lab classification ('NR n78/n79, no commercial identity') is correct.

The 'dual-band' / multi-band files are REAL measured frequencies, but they mix serving cell + redirect target + NSA secondary carrier, not multiple simultaneous serving cells. In the B7+B28 files (e.g. normal_2026_04_13_14_34_31) EARFCN 9410 (B28, 700 MHz) appears via lte-rrc_dl_carrierfreq inside a System Information message = the actual serving carrier, while EARFCN 3200 (B7, 2600 MHz) appears via lte-rrc_carrierfreq inside an RRCConnectionRelease = a redirect/reselection target (redirectedCarrierInfo). In the 5-band file (B1/3/5/7/28) the NR EARFCNs 275/1350/2500 appear via lte-rrc_carrierfreq inside RRCConnectionReconfiguration = NR secondary-cell config for 5G-NSA dual connectivity. These all reflect real SKT deployment (SKT runs LTE on B1/B3/B5/B7/B28), so multi-band is a real data property, not a config artifact.

Empty / near-empty captures are real but information-poor, not corrupt. Two 1-row files (normal_2026_04_18_04_06_14, normal_2026_04_27_16_45_46) each contain exactly one valid LTE 'paging' RRC PDU (cn_domain, pagingRecordList, s_tmsi populated). normal_2026_05_06_17_26_33 has 2 paging rows. These carry no operator identity (plmn operator = None) and are classified commercial only via the default-band rule, so their commercial label rests on assumption, not direct evidence. The smallest meaningful capture with identity is normal_2026_04_21_17_59_47 (5 rows: RRCConnection Request/Setup/Setup Complete plus Detach request, SKT 450/05 via NAS).

corrections.correct: They are 3G/UMTS captures. origin_records.json already labels all nine rat_label '3G (UMTS)', and the raw info column carries UTRAN RRC PDU names (MIB, Sys Info Type SB1/1/3/5/11, rrc Connection Request/Setup/Release, paging Type1). 'Unknown' only reflects that the CSV schema lacks UMTS-RRC columns so none of the four schema RAT flags fire.

corrections.claimed: All normal_mixed* files are among the 24 NR-without-commercial test/lab files
corrections.correct: normal_mixed3 and normal_mixed5 are LTE-only (zero nr-rrc_* columns populated; info is just 'paging' x6-7 plus 'measurement Report' x2-3), so the NR-without-identity rule cannot apply to them. origin_records.json correctly classifies both as commercial (rat_label 'LTE (EPS)', origin_reason 'LTE on commercial bands, attach not captured'), which contradicts the blanket 'normal_mixed* = test' statement.

caveats: The 16 h duration of normal_2026_04_20_14_35_18 is genuine elapsed time but is NOT 16 h of dense traffic: it is an intermittent paging-mostly DIAG session with multi-minute idle gaps (largest 277.8 s). Treat it as a long sparse capture, not a high-rate one.

One file, normal_2026_05_14_15_22_36, has 2 sub-millisecond backward timestamp steps (~200 microseconds). These are DIAG log-ordering artifacts where an inner NAS PDU (Attach request, Identity response) is stamped just before its RRC container (RRCConnectionSetupComplete, ulInformationTransfer), not a real clock reversal. They do not affect duration_s but mean strict per-row monotonicity is not 100% guaranteed.

The commercial label on the smallest files (the two 1-row paging files, the 2-row file, and the seven identity-less 3G files) is inferential, resting on the default-band rule rather than on any captured operator identity (no gummei, no full IMSI, no foreign paging). Statistically they are commercial but they carry no in-file proof.

The 5G-only file's NR SIB1 exposes only the unreliable per-digit nr-rrc mcc_show=3 / mnc_show=2 fragments (bit-field pieces, not a real PLMN '3/2'). Per CLAUDE memory and the task rules these per-digit lte/nr-rrc MCC/MNC fields are not trustworthy for operator identity; the test/lab call rests on absence of gummei/IMSI plus NR-only content, which is sound.

Band/EARFCN-to-band mapping in origin_records.json comes only from LTE EARFCNs (lte-rrc carrierfreq fields); the CSV has no NR carrier ARFCN column, so NR n78/n79 testbed presence is inferred from 'NR present with no commercial identity', and any NR serving frequency cannot be band-verified directly.

I examined 4 of the 9 3G files in raw form in depth (the two foreign-paging ones plus two SIB/connection ones) and relied on origin_records.json top_info/info for the other 5; all 9 share the same UTRAN PDU vocabulary, so the 3G conclusion holds, but only 4 were byte-level verified.

sections.overview:
Origin overview

The normal set is 133 benign captures recorded as the baseline for a UE-side false base station detector. These captures come from two distinct origins. 103 are commercial captures taken on real South Korean live networks, and 30 are lab captures produced on an srsRAN plus Open5GS testbed driven by a LibreSDR B220 mini. The aggregate splits exactly as 103 commercial against 30 test/lab.

The test set is identified by any one of three lab fingerprints. The first is the test PLMN 00101 seen in the gummei. The second is LTE Band 8 (900 MHz) with no commercial identity. The third is an NR signal present without any commercial identity, which stands in for an n78 or n79 testbed capture because the CSV schema carries no NR carrier ARFCN to bind the NR leg to an operator. A real commercial identity always overrides the band rule. A serving PLMN of 450/05 (SK Telecom) or 450/08 (KT), or paging of foreign-roamer IMSIs that a single 00101 SIM could never page, marks a capture commercial even when it also touches Band 8 or carries NR. The 30 test/lab captures break down as 4 identified by PLMN 00101, 3 by LTE Band 8, and 23 by NR without a commercial identity. The commercial reasons break down as 58 LTE on commercial bands with the attach not captured, 39 on SK Telecom (450/05), 4 by foreign-roamer paging on a live cell, and 1 on KT (450/08).

By radio access technology the set is 90 LTE (EPS), 33 5G-NSA (LTE plus NR), 9 3G (UMTS), and 1 standalone 5G, which sum to the full 133. The commercial captures were collected on rooted Qualcomm phones (OnePlus 9 Pro, Samsung S20 and S22) running the MODI app through diag_mdlog in Seoul, with the capturing UE roaming on a Globe Philippines SIM. The two operators actually observed in-capture are SK Telecom (39 files) and KT (1 file), with 93 files exposing no PLMN in the capture itself. Across the set the captures total 37,127 packets over 94,803.2 seconds of elapsed session time. Together these 133 captures form the benign baseline that a UE-side false base station detector is calibrated and tested against.
sections.rf_cell:
Radio origin: cells, bands, tracking areas

The base-station evidence in these captures comes almost entirely from the serving cell's system-information broadcasts. The MODI app records the SIB1 and other System Information Block messages the phone decodes while camping, so each capture carries the cell's own published identity, frequency, tracking area, and camping thresholds. Of the 133 files, 86 expose at least one LTE carrier frequency and 87 expose a tracking area code, while the remaining files hold only paging or connection messages with no SIB content.

The frequency evidence is the LTE EARFCN, which maps to a band. The records observe 14 distinct serving and neighbour EARFCNs plus two measurement-carrier values. Band 28 (700 MHz) is carried by EARFCN 9410, Band 7 (2600 MHz) by 2850 and 3200, Band 1 (2100 MHz) by 100, 275 and 475, Band 8 (900 MHz) by 3600, 3650 and 3743, Band 3 (1800 MHz) by 1350, 1550 and 1694, and Band 5 (850 MHz) by 2500 and 2600. Two further values, 10737 and 10836, come from the inter-frequency measurement carrier field, not from a serving cell, and they fall outside every LTE FDD downlink range, so they map to no band and must not be read as serving frequencies. One reference note: EARFCN 9410 on Band 28 has a downlink centre of 778.0 MHz, computed from the EARFCN with the TS 36.101 formula, which does not change any band assignment or origin verdict.

The band distribution below counts files, so a file that measures more than one band is counted in each. The 86 files with band data produce 150 file-band observations. Band 7 and Band 28 dominate, which matches an SK Telecom footprint that runs LTE on B1, B3, B5, B7 and B28. The multi-band files reflect a real serving carrier plus redirect or neighbour-measurement targets, not several simultaneous serving cells.

Cell identity appears in two forms. The eNB cell identity, the 28-bit cellIdentity from SIB1, is present in 87 files with 63 distinct values. The physical cell ID, the layer-1 PCI that distinguishes neighbours on the same frequency, is present in 52 files with 34 distinct values ranging across the full 0 to 503 space (observed values include 0, 1, 2, 105, 184, 259 and higher). A separate target physical cell ID, naming a handover or reselection target, appears in 6 files with 19 distinct values. A single capture exposes one NR cell identity (value 75) from a 5G secondary leg. Because the schema has no NR carrier frequency column, an NR cell cannot be tied to a band or operator from the data.

Tracking area codes come from the LTE-RRC SIB broadcast and from EPS NAS. The LTE-RRC tracking area code is present in 87 files with 22 distinct values (such as 03, 07, 53 through 64). The EPS NAS tracking area identity, the full TAI carried in NAS attach and accept messages, appears in 14 files with 54 distinct values. No 5GS NAS tracking area is exposed in any file.

Cell-selection parameters, also broadcast in SIB1, are present in 87 files for the minimum receive level and 86 for reselection priority. The q-RxLevMin field takes eight magnitudes (55, 57, 61, 62, 64, 65, 66, 70), which decode to minimum receive levels of -110, -114, -122, -124, -128, -130, -132 and -140 dBm. The cellBarred flag is 1 (notBarred) in every file that carries it, meaning each captured cell was open for camping. Cell reselection priority spans the full range 0 through 7, and the default paging cycle takes values 0, 1 and 2. These broadcast thresholds confirm that the captures are camping on live, unbarred cells and reading their published selection rules rather than synthesising them.
sections.security_identity:
Security configuration and subscriber identities

Security material is present in 61 of the 133 normal captures, which is the subset that recorded an attach or registration exchange where the network advertises and selects its algorithms. The remaining files are paging-only or system-information-only captures with no security context exposed.

NAS and AS security algorithms. The 4G captures advertise a consistent LTE algorithm set. Sixty files carry the full EPS list of confidentiality algorithms 128-EEA1, 128-EEA2, EEA3, plus the null cipher EEA0, alongside integrity algorithms 128-EIA1, 128-EIA2, and EIA3. The null cipher EEA0 is advertised in all 60 of those files, which is expected because EEA0 is the mandatory fallback in the EPS algorithm bitmap and is offered for unciphered emergency or pre-authentication messages, not selected for normal traffic. No file advertises null integrity. The string EIA0 (null integrity) does not appear in any capture, and 5G-IA0 does not appear either, so integrity protection is always offered with a real algorithm. A single 5G standalone file (normal_5g_session_72) advertises the 5G algorithm set 128-5G-EA1, 128-5G-EA2, 128-5G-EA3 for confidentiality and 128-5G-IA1, 128-5G-IA2, 128-5G-IA3 for integrity, plus the null cipher 5G-EA0. This is the only file exposing 5G NAS algorithm advertisement, consistent with it being the only 5G-SA session in the set.

NAS security-header types. EPS NAS security headers (TS 24.301) are observed across the captures with the protected values dominating. The plain header type 0 appears in 48 files, integrity-protected type 1 in 2 files, integrity-protected-and-ciphered type 2 in 46 files, type 3 in 1 file, and integrity-protected-and-ciphered-with-new-context type 4 in 23 files. Type 2 is the steady-state protected header for live traffic and its broad presence matches the commercial attach captures. The single 5G-SA file shows 5GS security-header types 0 and 2. Numeric values above 4 that also appear in the raw field (such as 11, 12, 14, 15) are not valid security-header types. They are message-type or protocol-discriminator bytes captured when the high nibble is misaligned for plain NAS messages, so only values 0 through 4 are counted as header types here.

Message authentication codes. A NAS message authentication code is present in 51 of the 133 files. The MAC appears wherever the capture recorded integrity-protected NAS messages (security-header types 1, 2, 3, or 4), confirming that integrity protection is actually applied on the wire and not merely advertised.

Subscriber identities and the privacy gap

Identity types in use. Identities are dominated by temporary identifiers, which is the expected privacy-preserving behavior on live cells. Commercial captures expose S-TMSI in 41 files, M-TMSI in 40 files, and a full IMSI in 47 files. Test/lab captures expose S-TMSI in 27 files, M-TMSI in 4 files, and a 5G-TMSI in 1 file (the 5G-SA session). No file in either group exposes a SUCI (concealed 5G identity) or an IMEISV. The single lab file reporting an IMSI is normal_2026_05_14_14_31_43, whose paged IMSI decodes to SK Telecom 450/05. By the rule that a real 450/xx identity wins over the band rule, that file is a commercial capture that the current origin_records still labels test/lab. Setting that one aside, the lab captures carry no IMSI at all, only temporary identifiers and one 5G-TMSI.

Foreign-roamer paging is the key privacy distinction. The clearest separation between the two origins is in paged third-party identities. In 16 commercial files the cell pages real IMSIs belonging to subscribers other than the auditor UE, 33 paged foreign-roamer IMSIs in total. These IMSIs span at least 11 foreign home networks, including Japan (SoftBank and NTT DoCoMo), China (MCC 460), Hong Kong (MCC 454), Indonesia (MCC 510), Sri Lanka (MCC 413), Uzbekistan (MCC 434), Thailand (MCC 520), Vietnam (MCC 452), Netherlands (MCC 204), and Italy (MCC 222), alongside domestic Korean 450 subscribers. None of the 30 test/lab captures page a single foreign-roamer IMSI. A testbed provisioned with one 00101 SIM on an Open5GS core physically cannot page subscribers it never registered, so the presence of dozens of foreign home-network IMSIs is positive evidence of a live commercial cell and the absence of any is consistent with the isolated lab. The lab paging that does occur is by temporary S-TMSI only, with no IMSI revealed.

Operator identity. Operator identity, read only from the reliable e212 gummei and full IMSI fields, resolves to SK Telecom (450/05) in 39 files and KT (450/08) in 1 file. The remaining 93 files show no PLMN in the capture, which is why most commercial labels rest on the commercial-band rule rather than on a captured operator identity. The auditor UE itself carries the Globe PH IMSI 515027302508642 and appears as a known roaming identity in the captures, separate from the third-party subscribers described above.
sections.groups:
Activity groups

The 133 normal captures fall into seven filename groups. Counts come from the origin_records.json aggregate by_group block. The origin and RAT splits below were recomputed per group from the per-file records. The two origins are 103 commercial and 30 test/lab across the whole set.

GroupCountOriginNotes
Timestamped DIAG session 67 67 commercial The main field-collection group, files named by capture date and time. RAT mix is 48 LTE (EPS), 10 5G-NSA, and 9 3G (UMTS). These carry the live commercial evidence, SK Telecom and KT serving PLMN, Paging Type1 of many third-party and foreign-roamer subscriber IMSIs, real cell identities, and commercial EARFCNs on bands B1, B3, B5, B7, B8, and B28. One NR capture here (2026_05_14_14_31_43) pages a real SK Telecom subscriber, so it is commercial too.
LTE batch 2026-03-18 23 23 commercial Files named normal_3_18_26_lte_*, all LTE (EPS). Entirely commercial. Signalling is LTE RRC system information and paging on commercial bands, with attach not always captured, so most carry no in-file PLMN but sit on commercial EARFCNs.
Mixed activity 18 12 test/lab, 6 commercial Files named normal_mixed*. RAT mix is 13 5G-NSA and 5 LTE. The 12 test/lab files show NR-RRC present with no commercial PLMN and paging by S-TMSI only, the n78/n79 testbed signature. The 6 commercial files carry SK Telecom or KT PLMN, and two of them (mixed3, mixed5) are LTE-only with no NR.
Data session 13 7 test/lab, 6 commercial Files named normal_data and normal_data2 through normal_data13, all LTE (EPS). The test/lab files are flagged by PLMN 00101 (data, data2, data6, data7) or LTE Band 8 with no commercial identity (data3, data4, data5). The remaining files sit on commercial bands and are commercial.
UDP streaming 7 6 test/lab, 1 commercial Files named udp_streaming*. RAT mix is 6 5G-NSA and 1 LTE. The 6 test/lab files are NR present with no commercial identity, S-TMSI paging on the testbed. They also show measured LTE neighbour bands, which are inter-frequency reports rather than serving cells.
VoLTE call 4 4 test/lab Files named voltecall*, all 5G-NSA. All four are test/lab, NR present with no commercial PLMN and no foreign paging. Signalling is LTE anchor RRC plus NR secondary-cell configuration with S-TMSI paging.
5G session 1 1 test/lab Single file normal_5g_session_72, the only 5G standalone capture. NAS-5GS registration and deregistration with NR-RRC MIB, SIB1, setup and release. No LTE anchor, no gummei PLMN, no full IMSI, so it is the cleanest n78/n79 testbed 5G-SA capture.

In short, the LTE batch and the timestamped DIAG sessions are almost entirely commercial and carry the live-network evidence. The VoLTE call and 5G session groups are entirely test/lab. Mixed activity, data session, and UDP streaming are split, with the testbed files identified by PLMN 00101, LTE Band 8, or NR present with no commercial identity, while commercial files in those groups win on a real 450/xx PLMN or foreign-roamer paging.

Note. normal_2026_05_14_14_31_43 (timestamped DIAG session) pages a real SK Telecom subscriber IMSI (450050746404373), which an isolated 00101 testbed core cannot do, so it is classed commercial. The final split is 103 commercial and 30 test/lab, with 23 NR-without-identity test files.

key_findings: The normal set is 133 captures from two origins: ~102 (after the one correction below, 103) from real commercial Korean networks and ~31 (corrected to 30) from a private srsRAN + Open5GS + LibreSDR B220 mini testbed; the split is recorded in origin_records.json aggregate.by_origin_class.

Commercial captures were taken in Seoul on rooted Qualcomm handsets (OnePlus 9 Pro, Samsung S20/S22) via the MODI diag_mdlog pipeline; the auditing UE itself roams on a Globe Philippines SIM (own IMSI 515027302508642, MCC 515/02), so the auditor identity is foreign to the Korean cells it observes.

The only operators positively identified come from trustworthy fields (e212_gummei and full e212_imsi): SK Telecom (MCC/MNC 450/05) in 39 files plus 1 KT (450/08); 93 files expose no PLMN at all and are classed commercial only by the default commercial-band rule (origin_reason 'LTE on commercial bands, attach not captured', 58 files) rather than by captured operator identity.

RAT mix spans four generations: 90 LTE (EPS), 33 5G-NSA (LTE+NR, EPS NAS, no 5GS NAS), 1 true 5G-SA (normal_5g_session_72, 5GS NAS present, no LTE anchor), and 9 3G/UMTS captures that upstream tooling mislabels 'unknown' only because the CSV schema has no UMTS-RRC columns (their info rows carry genuine UTRAN PDU names: MIB, Sys Info Type, rrc Connection Request/Setup/Release, paging Type1).

Testbed identity is established by ANY of: PLMN 00101 (4 files: normal_data/data2/data6/data7), LTE Band 8 with no commercial identity (3 files: normal_data3/data4/data5, pure EARFCN 3600), or NR present with no bindable commercial identity standing in for an n78/n79 capture (NR-no-identity bucket); a captured 450/xx PLMN or foreign-roamer IMSI paging always overrides the band rule and marks a capture commercial.

Genuine commercial origin is proven for foreign-roamer paging: live SKT/KT cells page subscriber IMSIs from Japan (440), China (460), Hong Kong (454), Indonesia (510), Thailand (520), Sri Lanka (413), Vietnam (452) and Uzbekistan (434) alongside Korean 450 subscribers; a single provisioned 00101 testbed SIM on an isolated Open5GS core physically cannot page roamers it never registered.

Only 10 NR-bearing files (9 SKT 450/05 + 1 KT 450/08 via normal_mixed17) are genuine commercial 5G-NSA; the rest of the NR captures lack any bindable operator and are testbed, so the ground-truth brief's '11 commercial NR files' is off by one.

Multi-band observations are real measured frequencies, not config artifacts, but mix serving cell, redirect/reselection targets (lte-rrc_carrierfreq inside RRCConnectionRelease), and NSA secondary-carrier configs (inside RRCConnectionReconfiguration); they reflect real SKT deployment on B1/B3/B5/B7/B28 (band tallies: B7 x54, B28 x50, B1 x19, B8 x13, B3 x11, B5 x3).

Subscriber-privacy exposure is significant on commercial cells: paging records leak thousands of S-TMSIs (e.g. normal_2026_04_20_14_35_18 pages 4411 distinct S-TMSIs over a genuine 16.2 h session) and dozens of cleartext IMSIs of foreign roamers, captured passively by a UE-side auditor.

The single 5G-SA and the NR-only testbed files carry no gummei and no full IMSI, exposing only a 5G-TMSI and unreliable per-digit NR-RRC MCC/MNC fragments, consistent with an isolated lab core rather than a live operator.
corrections_applied: Reclassify normal_2026_05_14_14_31_43.csv from test/lab ('NR n78/n79, no commercial identity') to COMMERCIAL: raw CSV row 12 is an LTE paging message carrying e212_imsi 450050746404373 (MCC 450 MNC 05 = SK Telecom), a third-party subscriber distinct from the auditor's 515/02 SIM; a 00101 testbed cannot page an SKT subscriber by IMSI. This shifts the true split to 103 commercial / 30 test/lab and the NR-no-identity bucket from 24 to 23. The origin_records.json imsi_analysis pipeline failed to extract this paged IMSI (distinct_imsi recorded as None, foreign_paged 0).

Fix EARFCN 9410 center frequency: origin_records.json stores center_mhz 783.0 for all 50 files, but TS 36.101 Table 5.7.3-1 Band 28 (FDL_low 758.0 MHz, NOffs-DL 9210) gives 758.0 + 0.1*(9410-9210) = 778.0 MHz; 783.0 corresponds to EARFCN 9460. Band assignment B28 and nominal '700 MHz' are correct, only the center MHz is wrong by +5 MHz (cosmetic, does not change any origin verdict).

Correct the ground-truth count of commercial NR files from 11 to 10 (9 SKT 450/05 + 1 KT 450/08 = normal_mixed17); no 11th commercial file carries any NR or NAS-5GS signal. The 102/31 totals in origin_records.json remain internally consistent.

Do not read measurement-carrier values 10737 and 10836 (from lte-rrc_carrierfreq, the SIB inter-frequency/measurement field) as serving cells; they fall outside every LTE FDD DL EARFCN range in TS 36.101 so band=None is the only honest mapping. The records correctly use band=None but mix these into the same 'bands' list as serving dl_carrierfreq values, which can mislead.

Reject the blanket 'all normal_mixed* = NR test/lab' statement: normal_mixed3 and normal_mixed5 are LTE-only (zero NR-RRC columns populated) and are correctly classed commercial ('LTE on commercial bands, attach not captured'), so the NR-without-identity rule cannot apply to them.

Relabel the '9 unknown RAT' files as 3G/UMTS captures (origin_records.json already carries rat_label '3G (UMTS)'); 'unknown' only reflects the CSV schema lacking UMTS-RRC columns so none of the four schema RAT flags fire.
caveats: Operator identity is reliable ONLY from e212_gummei and full e212_imsi (BCD-with-f-filler: 00f1/f110 => 001/01, 54f0 => 450); per-digit lte-rrc/nr-rrc mcc/mnc fields are bit-field fragments and were NOT used for operator identity. The single 5G-SA file's NR SIB1 mcc_show=3/mnc_show=2 are such unreliable fragments, not a real PLMN.

93 of 133 files expose no PLMN in-capture, so most commercial labels (the 58 'attach not captured' files plus the two 1-row paging files, the 2-row file, and 7 identity-less 3G files) rest on the default commercial-band rule and dataset-owner provenance, not on captured operator identity; they carry no in-file proof of being commercial.

The 23 NR-no-identity testbed labels are defensible but NOT airtight: several files page dozens of distinct S-TMSIs (up to 57 in normal_mixed16) and measure live commercial LTE bands, which is more consistent with a busy live 5G-NSA cell whose LTE-anchor PLMN was simply not captured than with a quiet single-SIM lab. The label survives only because the CSV schema cannot bind the NR leg to an operator and none of these files carry a 450/xx gummei or any IMSI; high-paging files (mixed16/9/18, udp_streaming5/7, voltecall4) are the weakest test labels.

The CSV schema has NO NR carrier ARFCN/freqband column, so NR captures cannot be bound to a serving NR frequency or operator; n78/n79 testbed presence is inferred from 'NR present with no commercial identity', and no NR serving frequency can be band-verified directly.

Band classification must read the EARFCN _show column (decimal); the _value column is raw ASN.1-encoded bytes and a naive parse mislabels bands (e.g. Band 8 as Band 4). The lte-rrc_dl_carrierfreq_showname display value (e.g. '786' for EARFCN 9410) is a separate parser artifact and is not authoritative.

The per-file timestamp is a relative capture clock in seconds starting at 0.0, so duration_s = max-min timestamp is elapsed session time, not wall-clock; the 16.2 h outlier is genuine but sparse (paging-mostly, idle gaps up to 277.8 s). One file (normal_2026_05_14_15_22_36) has two sub-millisecond backward steps from DIAG log-ordering, so strict per-row monotonicity is not 100% guaranteed.

3GPP decodes (EARFCN->band, q-RxLevMin = -2*stored magnitude, nas-eps security_header_type 0-4, cellBarred 1=notBarred) were verified by recomputation against TS 36.101/36.331/24.301 from knowledge, not from a live spec PDF; field shownames in these CSVs are mostly numeric parser node IDs, not human-readable text, so decodes were validated against the numeric show/value codes plus spec. nas-eps_security_header_type values >4 (5,6,8,11,12,14,15) in the raw data are misaligned EMM message-type bytes, not extra security-header types.

Only a subset of files were byte-level re-verified (all 3 Band-8, all 4 PLMN-00101, all NR-test, the 5G-SA file, all 10 commercial NR files, 4 of 9 3G files); the 58 'attach not captured' and 39 pure-LTE SKT labels were taken as given beyond a paging spot-check.
